tensor.c_T_caveat: In general Horndeski with G_5 ≠ 0, tensor propagation is not determined by G_4 alone on all backgrounds. Full TEP solution requires complete quadratic perturbation equations.
tensor.structural_reason: G_4 = M_Pl²/2 is constant, so c_T = 1 on the Schwarzschild benchmark. G_5 may modify tensor propagation on non-Schwarzschild backgrounds.
tensor.G5_note: G_5 does not enter the G_4-only tensor speed formula, but in general Horndeski the G_5 term couples tensor perturbations to the background scalar gradient. Published EsGB perturbation analyses derive background-dependent speeds.

scalar.scalar_kinetic_sign: K_S = -X > 0 for timelike gradient (X < 0) → no scalar ghost
scalar.scalar_speed: c_S² = 1 on the background metric (G_{4φ} = 0, canonical kinetic)
scalar.G5_effect: G_5 modifies the background scalar profile and scalar-tensor mixing, but not c_S directly

birefringence.birefringence_general: b ~ α_GB * G_{5X} / G_4 * (shear) ≠ 0 on non-spherical backgrounds (O(α_GB))
birefringence.key_result: b = 0 on all spherically symmetric backgrounds (including Schwarzschild + scalar hair)

matter_photon.coupling_order: O(η) for massive particles (conformal factor), O(η²) for photons (metric correction only)

frame_split_signature.ISCO: O(η) — massive particles feel A = e^{-φ}
frame_split_signature.QNM: O(η²) — tensor on g, background correction

frame_dictionary.key_insight: The three characteristic metrics are structurally distinct: tilde_g (matter), g (tensor), g^scalar (temporal). The frame-split is the different coupling orders at which observables shift.

conclusions.ghost_free: Both tensor and scalar sectors are ghost-free
conclusions.frame_split: Three distinct characteristic metrics with different coupling orders
